description: Use Q for released energy in the proton–proton chain equation and define it immediately afterward, matching textbook notation.

changes.before: <exercise id="fs-id1430227" type="conceptual-questions"><problem id="fs-id1430227-revised-problem"><para id="fs-id1430227-revised-p1"><span id="fs-id1430227-extension"/>The net conversion in the proton–proton chain, including positron annihilation, can be written <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><m:mrow><m:mn>4</m:mn><m:mi>p</m:mi><m:mo>+</m:mo><m:mn>2</m:mn><m:msup><m:mi>e</m:mi><m:mo>−</m:mo></m:msup><m:mo>→</m:mo><m:mmultiscripts><m:mtext>He</m:mtext><m:mprescripts/><m:none/><m:mn>4</m:mn></m:mmultiscripts><m:mo>+</m:mo><m:mn>2</m:mn><m:msub><m:mi>ν</m:mi><m:mi mathvariant="italic">e</m:mi></m:msub><m:mo>+</m:mo><m:mtext>released energy</m:mtext></m:mrow></m:math>. Check electric charge and nucleon number. If <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>L</m:mi><m:mi>e</m:mi></m:msub></m:mrow></m:math> is +1 for an electron and an electron neutrino, check electron-family number too.</para></problem></exercise>
